svg.title: Comparing Alignment Methods
svg.desc: Eight small multiples of the same simulated sample of 24 noisy two-bump curves, whose true warps mix a shift, a change of tempo and a smooth bend, registered by eight methods: no alignment, iterative shift, affine, landmark, continuous (Ramsay-Li), elastic DP, elastic RBFGS with a penalty, and Tang-Mueller pairwise synchronisation (WFDA). Each panel shows ten registered curves and their cross-sectional mean, with the remaining variance as a fraction of the unregistered variance. Iterative shift (0.394) and WFDA (0.194) leave the most spread; affine, landmark, continuous and both elastic variants sharpen the mean, elastic DP the most, although the lowest variance is partly over-registration rather than better warps.
svg.text: One sample (shift + tempo + smooth bend), eight registrations; ten curves and the mean each
